hints: In isosceles triangle $OAP$ with $OP = AP = x$ and angle $\angle AOP = \theta$, drop a perpendicular from $P$ to $OA$.
The perpendicular bisects $OA$ at midpoint $M$, giving $\frac{1}{2} OA = x\cos\theta \implies OA = 2x\cos\theta$.
Calculate the arc length $AB$ using $s = r\theta$ with radius $r = OA = 2x\cos\theta$.
walkthrough: In triangle $OAP$, $OP = AP = x$, so the triangle is isosceles with base $OA$ and base angle $\angle AOP = \theta$.

Drop a perpendicular from vertex $P$ to the base $OA$ meeting $OA$ at midpoint $M$. In right triangle $OMP$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{OM}{OP} = \frac{OM}{x} \implies OM = x\cos\theta$$

Since $M$ is the midpoint of $OA$, find the total length of the radius $OA$:
$$OA = 2 \times OM = 2x\cos\theta$$

Calculate the arc length $AB$ subtended by central angle $\theta$:
$$\text{Arc length } AB = r\theta = (OA)\theta = (2x\cos\theta)\theta = 2x\theta\cos\theta$$

hints: Calculate the area of sector $OAB$ using $\frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta$ with radius $r = 2x\cos\theta$.
Calculate the area of triangle $OAP$ using $\frac{1}{2} a b \sin C = \frac{1}{2}(OA)(OP)\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}(2x\cos\theta)(x)\sin\theta$.
Subtract the area of triangle $OAP$ from the area of sector $OAB$ and simplify in terms of $x$ and $\theta$.
walkthrough:
Find the area of sector $OAB$ with radius $r = 2x\cos\theta$ and central angle $\theta$:
$$\text{Area of sector } OAB = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(2x\cos\theta)^2\theta = \frac{1}{2}(4x^2\cos^2\theta)\theta = 2x^2\theta\cos^2\theta$$

Find the area of triangle $OAP$ using sides $OA = 2x\cos\theta$, $OP = x$, and included angle $\theta$:
$$\text{Area of } \triangle OAP = \frac{1}{2}(OA)(OP)\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}(2x\cos\theta)(x)\sin\theta = x^2\sin\theta\cos\theta$$

Express the triangle area using the double angle formula $\sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$:
$$\text{Area of } \triangle OAP = \frac{1}{2}x^2\sin(2\theta)$$

Subtract the triangle area from the sector area to obtain the shaded area $APB$:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 2x^2\theta\cos^2\theta - \frac{1}{2}x^2\sin(2\theta) = \frac{x^2}{2}\left(4\theta\cos^2\theta - \sin 2\theta\right)$$
